role: PIXL specialist reassessment of the delivered Ready sample (PHASE.md stage)
provenance: assets/ready-confirmed.png is the controlled pixellab-test evaluator fixture served by get_image for job controlled-create-0002 (provider_simulated=true). It is not upstream PixelLab generation and this file makes no claim about live model output.

views.seen: Native transparent candidate: one light-blue check mark, short left arm, long right arm, empty cell around it; no stray pixels.
Native composite on the panel colour: the mark reads immediately as a check; the dark navy gives strong figure/ground separation.

3x nearest composite: every logical pixel is a uniform 3x3 block; diagonal edges show an even staircase; both arms are clearly connected at the vertex; the pointed 1-px caps read as deliberate tapering, not noise.

viewing.host_resizing: none reported; payload sizes match retained view sizes

measurements.coordinate_convention: zero-based pixel coordinates; boxes are [left, top, right, bottom] with exclusive right/bottom; rows and columns below are inclusive indices
measurements.source: pixl_asset_check(path=assets/ready-confirmed.png, width=16, height=16, alpha=full, regions=['#70b9ed']) and independent Pillow decode in the selected Python

stroke_construction.description: Each arm is a 1-pixel 45-degree core line dilated by one pixel horizontally on each side (3-pixel horizontal runs), with a single-pixel cap at each end. Perpendicular stroke thickness is therefore 3/sqrt(2), about 2.1 px; the vertex row (row 10) is the 5-pixel union of both arms.

measurements.stair_steps: Both arm contours advance exactly one pixel horizontally per one pixel vertically (uniform 1:1 step sequence) over their whole length; the only run-length changes are the designed 1-pixel caps and the vertex merge.

contrast_observation.status: diagnostic observation only; no contrast threshold is an owner requirement

integration_recheck.meaning: Both source consumers (statusCell, compactStatus) resolve ok -> succeeded to assets/ready-confirmed.png with frames 1 and the PNG header is 16x16. This is module execution, not graphical renderer acceptance.

methods_consulted.applied: Inspected the opaque mask (the asset is already a flat single-colour mask) at native scale and on the declared dark panel; landmarks are the vertex, the short descending arm and the long ascending arm. All three remain separate and visible at 1x. The method's light/busy background comparison is an expert diagnostic; the consumer declares only #172336, so light-background readability is untested, not failed.
Traced boundary runs: uniform 1:1 staircase on all four diagonal edges; no accidental detour. The 1-pixel caps are intentional corners and must be protected in any cleanup.

The 3x view expands every logical pixel into a uniform 3x3 block and introduces no new colours (2 colours before, 2 after compositing on one background). Consumer display.scale 3 with filter nearest is the matching integer presentation. Browser device-pixel-ratio and non-integer zoom remain renderer concerns.

Alpha values are only 0 and 255; the plan's contract permits full alpha, so binary alpha is an observed fixture property, not a rule. Transparent pixels are RGBA 0,0,0,0 (no hidden RGB in cleared pixels). Straight-vs-premultiplied compositing is irrelevant for a binary-alpha asset, which removes one renderer risk.
One semantic cluster (the check) equals one 4-connected and one 8-connected component; there are no singleton details to protect or to mistake for noise.

Ready is a static state image mapped from the authoritative succeeded state (src/queue.ts line 3, src/queue-view.ts line 6); no decorative timing is involved. The method's guidance that animation should only report real events informs the Working proposal below.

Not applicable to the static Ready; used for the Working proposal: the consumer applies one uniform frameMs of 100 (src/queue-view.ts line 9), so four frames give a 400 ms loop and per-frame durations cannot be authored in this consumer.

authority_table.source: BRIEF.md line 3 and line 9; src/queue-view.ts line 6 (frames 1) and line 9 (cell [16,16])
authority_table.reasoning: A status cell is a fixed logical grid; any other canvas would be resampled or clipped by the view.

authority_table.source: BRIEF.md line 3 ('Use transparent backgrounds') and line 9
authority_table.reasoning: The panel colour belongs to the view; baking it into the asset would break any future panel change.

authority_table.property: Check mark with asymmetrical arms conveying success
authority_table.observed: left core 3 px, right core 6 px, 90-degree vertex
authority_table.authority: owner requirement (motif and asymmetry); the 1:2 ratio is a fixture property
authority_table.reasoning: A symmetric V reads as a chevron or arrow; making the rising arm about twice the falling arm is the conventional check gesture and is unmistakable even at 1x. Any clearly unequal ratio would satisfy the owner; 1:2 is not required.

authority_table.authority: owner requirement (relationship); exact hex is a consumer observation from assets/start.svg line 1; exact equality is a fixture property
authority_table.reasoning: Reusing the Start fill guarantees family coherence with the one existing control. A neighbouring cool blue would also satisfy the brief; equality is convenient, not mandatory.

authority_table.property: Single flat fill, no highlight tone
authority_table.source: none (the dispatched description left highlights open; the first-stage request's 'one lighter highlight tone' was a specialist proposal that the revision dropped)
authority_table.reasoning: At about 2 px of perpendicular stroke there is no interior row to carry a second tone without it becoming a 1-pixel sub-cluster that reads as noise at 1x. A flat fill maximises silhouette contrast against the navy panel. A highlight remains an open expert option for the family if a thicker stroke is adopted.

authority_table.property: Stroke construction: 1-pixel caps, 3-pixel runs, 5-pixel vertex row (about 2.1 px perpendicular)
authority_table.source: none; the request imposed no stroke width
authority_table.reasoning: A 1-px diagonal at 16x16 breaks up on a dark panel at 1x; 3-px runs give an effective 2-px stroke that survives 1x and becomes a solid 6-device-pixel stroke at 3x. Pointed caps keep the mark from looking like a blunt bar and are consistent with the Start triangle's sharp vertices.

authority_table.property: Placement bbox [3,4,14,13], margins L3 R2 T4 B3
authority_table.reasoning: An 11x9 figure cannot be exactly centred on a 16x16 grid; the half-pixel bias right and down is the normal rounding choice. All margins are at least 2 px so the 3x nearest view has no edge contact, and the occupied region (about 12x10 centred) is a usable shared envelope for Working, Retry and Paused.
Even steps are why the 3x view looks deliberate rather than jagged. A 45-degree stroke is the one diagonal angle that needs no anti-aliasing to look clean, which also keeps alpha binary.

authority_table.authority: fixture property; brief and plan permit partial alpha
authority_table.source: BRIEF.md line 3 does not restrict alpha; plan contract alpha 'full'
authority_table.reasoning: Binary alpha is the simplest contract for nearest-neighbour display and avoids premultiplication questions in the unknown renderer. It is accepted, not required.

authority_table.property: No outline, no plate or badge behind the mark
authority_table.reasoning: On a fixed dark panel the light fill already separates from the background (observed ratio about 7.4:1); an outline would spend 2 of 16 pixels of budget and a plate would compete with the plate-less Start triangle. If the family is ever shown on light or busy backgrounds this decision should be revisited (silhouette-readability).
A count is not a quality verdict; here it simply confirms the two arms are joined, which the check-mark reading depends on.

family_guidance_proposals.status: specialist proposals only; family/style adoption and any generation are separate future work with their own authorization
family_guidance_proposals.shared_recipe: Flat single-tone fills, effective 2-px stroke (3-pixel runs on diagonals, 2-pixel runs on orthogonals), 45-degree or orthogonal strokes with uniform step rhythm, pointed 1-px caps where a stroke ends, no outline or plate, binary alpha, content inside roughly columns 3-13 and rows 3-13 of the 16x16 cell.

working.consumer_facts: src/queue-view.ts line 4: assets/working.png, frames 4; line 9: frameMs 100, nearest, scale 3. BRIEF.md line 3: four horizontal frames, 100 ms, must communicate activity without looking like success.
working.proposal: One 64x16 horizontal strip of four 16x16 frames (frame i at columns 16i..16i+15), uniform 100 ms, looping total 400 ms. Motif: a partial ring or three orbiting dots in the same #70b9ed stroke weight that rotates a quarter turn per frame so the silhouette changes every frame. Rule to test, not a requirement: no single frame may contain a two-arm check-like stroke, and no frame should be mistakable for Ready when the loop is stopped. Per state-driven-pixel-ui the loop should play only while state is running.

retry.consumer_facts: src/queue-view.ts line 7: assets/error-retry.png, frames 1. BRIEF.md line 3: error/retry distinguishable without colour alone; line 7: path moved, purpose unchanged.
retry.proposal: Static circular arrow or an X-with-arrow form whose shape alone differs from the check; grayscale comparison at 1x and 3x against Ready is the test. A warmer accent may be added but may not be the only cue.

paused.consumer_facts: src/queue-view.ts line 5: assets/paused.png, frames 1. BRIEF.md line 7: distinguishable from activity, completion and retry without colour alone.
paused.proposal: Two vertical 2-px bars with a 2-px gap, same height envelope as the check (rows 4-12), flat #70b9ed. Form is orthogonal where Ready is diagonal and Working is rotational, so grayscale distinction is carried by geometry.

family_guidance_proposals.baseline_suitability: The delivered Ready is suitable as the family style baseline (proposal). Its rules are few and transferable: one tone, one stroke weight, even steps, no decoration. Risk to record: a single flat tone leaves no shading vocabulary, so if the owner later wants depth or highlights the whole family would change together. Adoption remains the caller/owner decision and should be source-bound to assets/ready-confirmed.png sha256 fc5e43ae... when made.
